During 1963 , the Office of Transportation initiated research into the possibilities of future high - speed rail passenger trans- portation linking the major cities of New York State .

...

Equally important are the planning and land - use implications of the potential benefits that modern rail transportation might offer toward easing future traffic demands on highway and air travel . In some areas of the State , the ever - increasing need for land on which to build express highways and airports is already causing severe problems for the public agencies responsible for providing these transportation facilities .

For its initial investigation into possible improved intercity rail service for New York State , the route between New York City and Binghamton was selected because the Southern Tier area has relatively less satisfactory alternate modes of travel to New York City and elsewhere . Pending the completion of Route 17 improvements , the Binghamton area is highly dependent on rail service , particularly so during periods of bad weather when roads are snow - covered and flying is limited .

The fastest rail service presently scheduled between New York City and Binghamton is four hours and twenty minutes for 192 miles . Preliminary investigation by this Office indicated that , for an initial phase operation using presently available equipment , it would be technically feasible to provide a limited stop service between these two points with a running time of about three - and - a - quarter hours . This would constitute a much more satisfactory travel time by today's standards of speed for other modes of transportation .

The results of this investigation were presented in July , 1963 ,... A committee was formed from this group to work with the Erie- Lackawanna Railroad to explore the possibilities of the plan .
